Apartment dwellers cannot regulate the heat in their home. 35% of the Russian food supply is grown on private plots by people who cannot afford to buy food in supermarkets. These people spend their summer weekends living in hot shacks called dachas while growing food (Russian propagandists pretend that the shacks are cute “summer
homes”). The average Russian home is 440 ft.², the size of a two car garage (the average American home is 2200 square feet; the average European home is about 1600 square feet). Because Russia is soaked in alcohol, it should be no surprise that it has the highest divorce rate in the world and the highest suicide rate of any large country. At the root of Russia’s problems is the fact that Russia has always been ruled by tyrants, creating a slave mentality among the population. Russia’s dictatorial rulers have held back the economic development of a country with immense natural resources that should be among the richest in the world. The Czars enslaved 90% of the country and turned a free peasantry into serfs. Half of the serfs were owned by private individuals while the other half were owned by the state. When the serfs were “freed” in 1861, they were forced to spend the next 47 years paying 1.6 billion rubles to the aristocracy for their freedom. Next came Joseph Stalin, the 20th century’s second most brutal tyrant. He murdered countless millions of Russians and created the famous Gulag (51% of Russians have a favorable view of Stalin!). Today, Russia is ruled by a madman who is attempting to reestablish the Russian empire in an age of ultranationalism. Putin has started a war of aggression that has killed or injured 2 million people and gone on longer than World War II. Some claim that Putin went to war to protect ethnic Russians in the Donbas. If this was true, Russia could have invaded just the Donbas instead of all of Ukraine. In fact, Putin‘s actual  motivation is perfectly clear. In 2021 he wrote a paper entitled “On the Historical Unity between Russians and Ukrainians” (available on the Internet under “Putin’s Mein Kampf”). In this paper, Putin made the fascistic argument that Ukrainians do not exist as a separate nationality, and have no right to independence. The Ukrainian nation has been victimized by Russia for 300 years and is now fighting to the death against the Russian Army, which largely consists of the rural Russian poor, but includes rapists and murderers from Russia’s prisons, North Korean slaves and African mercenaries. Because of this war, one million of Russia’s best and brightest have fled  the country. Russia’s population declined by 700,000 in 2025. Unsurprisingly, Russia is hated by all of its neighbors. In 1990, when the “prison house of nations” collapsed, 15 captive nations of obtained their freedom. Many of these countries joined NATO, a defensive alliance whose purpose is to protect Europe from Russian aggression. The Russian threat has become so severe since it invaded Ukraine that even traditionally neutral Sweden has joined NATO, along with Finland. Europe is being forced to re-arm at enormous expense. I do not write this because I hate Russia. I hate lies, half truths, propaganda and tyrants everywhere. I pity Russians because they are the victims of a cruel history. The source of most of my statistical information is Rosstat, the Russian government statistical service.
